logic_node.action: Conduct multidisciplinary discussion on cancer therapy management
logic_node.action_detail: In patients who develop cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy or HF, a multidisciplinary discussion involving the patient about the risk-benefit ratio of cancer therapy interruption, discontinuation, or continuation is recommended to improve management.

source_text: In patients who develop cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy or HF, a multidisciplinary discussion involving the patient about the risk-benefit ratio of cancer therapy interruption, discontinuation, or continuation is recommended to improve management.

logic_node.action: Initiate ARB, ACEi, or beta blocker for asymptomatic cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy
logic_node.action_detail: In asymptomatic patients with cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy (EF <50%), ARB, ACEi, and beta blockers are reasonable to prevent progression to HF and improve cardiac function.

source_text: In asymptomatic patients with cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy (EF <50%), ARB, ACEi, and beta blockers are reasonable to prevent progression to HF and improve cardiac function.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiovascular risk factors or known cardiac disease being considered for potentially cardiotoxic anticancer therapies, pretherapy evaluation of cardiac function is reasonable to establish baseline cardiac function and guide the choice of cancer therapy. Echocardiography is recommended as the first-line modality for LVEF assessment.

source_text: In patients with cardiovascular risk factors or known cardiac disease being considered for potentially cardiotoxic anticancer therapies, pretherapy evaluation of cardiac function is reasonable to establish baseline cardiac function and guide the choice of cancer therapy.

logic_node.action: Monitor cardiac function during cardiotoxic cancer therapy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiovascular risk factors or known cardiac disease receiving potentially cardiotoxic anticancer therapies, monitoring of cardiac function is reasonable for the early identification of drug-induced cardiomyopathy.

source_text: In patients with cardiovascular risk factors or known cardiac disease receiving potentially cardiotoxic anticancer therapies, monitoring of cardiac function is reasonable for the early identification of drug-induced cardiomyopathy.

logic_node.action: Consider beta blockers and ACEi/ARB for primary prevention of drug-induced cardiomyopathy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at risk of cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy, initiation of beta blockers and ACEi/ARB for the primary prevention of drug-induced cardiomyopathy is of uncertain benefit. Selected beta blockers studied include carvedilol and nebivolol. Spironolactone has also been investigated.

source_text: In patients at risk of cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy, initiation of beta blockers and ACEi/ARB for the primary prevention of drug-induced cardiomyopathy is of uncertain benefit.

logic_node.action: Consider serial cardiac troponin measurement for risk stratification
logic_node.action_detail: In patients being considered for potentially cardiotoxic therapies, serial measurement of cardiac troponin might be reasonable for further risk stratification. An elevated pretreatment troponin (>14 ng/L) was associated with a 4-fold increase in risk of cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy.

source_text: In patients being considered for potentially cardiotoxic therapies, serial measurement of cardiac troponin might be reasonable for further risk stratification.

logic_node.action_detail: Cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy is commonly defined as a decrease in LVEF of at least 10 percentage points to below 50%.

source_text: cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy commonly defined as a decrease in LVEF of at least 10% to <50%

logic_node.action: Discontinue cardiotoxic therapy and initiate GDMT workup
logic_node.action_detail: Patients who develop HF while receiving potentially cardiotoxic therapies should have these therapies discontinued while a diagnostic workup is undertaken to ascertain the cause of HF and initiate guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT).

source_text: Patients who develop HF while receiving potentially cardiotoxic therapies should have these therapies discontinued while a diagnostic workup is undertaken to ascertain the cause of HF and initiate GDMT.

logic_node.action: Initiate and uptitrate standard HF therapies for cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy
logic_node.action_detail: Initiation and uptitration of standard HF therapies (beta blockers, ACEi) remains the mainstay of treatment in patients with cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy or LVEF <50%, with close monitoring of cardiac function to guide discussions with oncology on the resumption of, or choice of, subsequent cancer therapies.

source_text: Initiation and uptitration of standard HF therapies remains the mainstay of treatment in patients with cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy or LVEF <50%, with close monitoring of cardiac function.

logic_node.action: Discontinue immune checkpoint inhibitors indefinitely for myocarditis
logic_node.action_detail: Patients diagnosed with immune checkpoint-related myocarditis typically have the offending agents (nivolumab, ipilimumab, pembrolizumab) discontinued indefinitely, given the associated high mortality.

source_text: patients diagnosed with immune checkpoint-related myocarditis typically have the offending agents discontinued indefinitely, given the associated high mortality.

logic_node.action: Consider enalapril if post-treatment troponin rises above threshold
logic_node.action_detail: In patients receiving high-dose chemotherapy with a post-treatment troponin rise >0.07 ng/mL, enalapril was effective in preventing significant LVEF decrease (>10% decrease to below 50%). None of the patients in the enalapril arm met the primary endpoint compared to 43% in the standard of care group.

source_text: 114 patients receiving high-dose chemotherapy and having a posttreatment troponin rise >0.07 ng/mL randomized to enalapril or placebo. None in enalapril arm met the primary endpoint (>10% decrease in LVEF to below 50%), while 43% of placebo group did.
